newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity Magellan trims bonds further in August.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity Magellan trims bonds further in August.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said Monday the manager of its Magellan Fund trimmed the mutual fund's massive holdings in bonds during August and raised its stake in technology stocks.

Magellan's multi-billion investment in bonds fell to 11.8 percent of the fund's assets at the end of August -- the most recent figures available -- from 15.6 percent at the end of July, according to the Fidelity Website (http://www.fid-inv.com).
Fund-watchers had expected manager Bob Stansky to move out of Magellan's controversial position in bonds, but he has been selling the stake at a slower pace than many analysts had expected.

Stansky took control of Magellan, the nation's largest mutual fund, in June following the sudden resignation of Jeffrey Vinik, whose push into U.S. bonds steered Magellan to its worst performance in years.

"It looks like (Stansky's) averaging out of the bonds. He's selling $50 (million) to $100 million a day," said David O'Leary, president of Alpha Equity Resarech Inc., a Portsmouth, N.H., fund research firm.
Analysts applauded Stansky's move out of bonds and into technology, but noted that the fund was still performing below average.
"I can't find a period in the last 25 years when Magellan's performance has been worse," O'Leary said.
Magellan under Stansky gained 1.67 percent during the third quarter, versus 3.09 percent for the Standard & Poor's index of 500 companies and 2.94 percent for the average growth company stock fund.
Assets in Magellan rose to $53.0 billion at the end of September from $51.7 billion at the end of August, but analysts said investors continued to sell the fund.
Michael DeMarco, a managing editor of Fidelity Independent Advisor, said he estimated that investors pulled out $800 million from Magellan in September.
"I think at some point the flow out of Magellan will stop and the fund should be a good buy again," he said.
Holdings in equities rose to 83.9 percent of assets at the end of August from 82.8 percent in July, while cash rose to 4.2 percent from 1.5 percent, Fidelity said.
Magellan's top 10 holdings remained unchanged, however U.S. bonds and Treasury notes fell from the top three positions to the first, fourth and seventh spots.
Also in the top 10 were Caterpillar Inc., General Motors Corp., Chrysler Corp., CSX Corp., Deere & Co., Royal Dutch Petroleum Co. and Exxon Corp.
Magellan's stake in technology stocks rose to 6.7 percent of assets in August from 5.5 percent at the end of July.
Energy stocks remained Magellan's top market sector, accounting for 13.0 percent of assets, down from 13.8 percent at the end of July.
Durables rose to 11.0 percent at the end of August from 10.8 percent, industrial machinery and equipment edged up to 9.4 percent from 9.2 percent, and finance rose to 7.2 percent from 7.0 percent.
